newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds dropped almost one full point at the close on Monday as a negative mood hit peripheral markets.
This was heightened in Spain by peseta weakness and Tuesday's Treasury auction, dealers said.
"What is worse is the general feeling that the correction is not over yet," said a dealer in Madrid.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended at 106 bps, from 92 bps at the close on Friday and dealers added it could widen even further tomorrow.
"People are taking their money abroad, so we're really likely to see (the spread) increasing," a dealer said.
A weaker peseta was proof of the shift in funds, he added.
The peseta was trading at around 84.99/85.00, on the verge of its ERM central parity rate of 85.0718 per mark and far off Friday's close at 84.70/72.
The market shrugged off continual central bank intervention to support the peseta, as dealers said that the Bank of Spain was only trying to smooth the currency's decline.
But the effect was evident on the yield curve, which flattened as earlier expectations of aggressive official rate cuts diminished.
No one now expects the Bank of Spain to move its key money rate at its regular repurchase auction tomorrow, dealers said.
